archetypes.name: commit-sequence
archetypes.rationale: The plan mandates A2-before-A1 commit ordering but lists files in A1-first order under 'Files to modify', creating an implementer confusion risk that could produce a transiently failing CI tree.
archetypes.prompt_body: Examine the plan's commit-ordering constraint: A2 timing-pin edits must land before or in the same commit as the A1 scanner to prevent a transiently failing CI tree. Verify that the 'Files to modify' section ordering (which lists test-implement-structure.sh before the launcher scripts) does not contradict the 'Approach' section directive, and assess whether the directive is unambiguous enough for the implementer to follow without prior context. Check whether the 'A2 before A1' guidance in the Approach section and the 'A1/A2 commit ordering' Failure Mode entry together provide a complete, non-contradictory ordering contract, or whether the plan relies on an unstated assumption about reading order. Identify any commit-sequence gap where an implementer following the 'Files to modify' list top-to-bottom could commit A1 before A2 and break CI. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: scanner-list-evidence
archetypes.rationale: The A1 scanner plan enumerates 15 production scripts by name; if any do not exist, lack timing calls, or are miscategorized as included or excluded, the scanner silently under-covers or false-positively fails CI.
archetypes.prompt_body: Inspect each of the 15 production scripts named in the A1 scanner explicit set (implement-bootstrap.sh, step2-implement.sh, commit-implementation.sh, commit-review-fixes.sh, step-7a.sh, refresh-run-logs.sh, implement-finalize.sh, step-telemetry-mark.sh, run-step5-review.sh, run-relevant-checks-captured.sh, launch-codex-implement.sh, launch-cursor-implement.sh, launch-codex-ci.sh, launch-cursor-ci.sh, launch-claude-ci.sh) and verify each exists at its stated path and contains at least one timing call matching the scanner's target subcommands (mark, record-vendor-task, or timing-report.sh invocation). The plan marks launch-claude-ci.sh as NEW under 'Files to modify' but also lists it in the scope-files.txt — check whether it already exists and whether the plan's treatment is consistent. Verify the exclusion list (launch-review.sh, launch-claude-subprocess.sh) is correct by checking whether those scripts actually contain timing calls that should or should not be pinned. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: doc-sync-scope
archetypes.rationale: The plan updates several .md contract files but explicitly exempts others; verify each exemption is sound and no in-scope contract file was overlooked given the actual behavior changes.
archetypes.prompt_body: Check the plan's doc-sync scope against repo evidence: it updates larch-log.md (D2/D4), python/README.md and scripts/lib-quiet.md (D3), and SECURITY.md (D4), and explicitly exempts test-implement-structure.md, launch-codex-implement.md, launch-cursor-implement.md, and test-larch-log-write-round.md from contract changes. Verify each exemption by checking whether those exempt files document behavior that the corresponding code changes actually alter. Also check whether any other .md contract file — such as scripts/larch-log-batches.md, launch-codex-ci.md, launch-cursor-ci.md, or launch-claude-ci.md — documents behavior touched by the plan's A2 launcher pinning changes and would be stale after implementation. Flag any .md contract the plan omits that would need updating to remain consistent with the new pinning behavior or D2/D4 comment rewording. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
